todos.content: Investigate why Goldfish app keeps restarting after quitting

input.command: launchctl list | grep -i goldfish 2>/dev/null; echo "---"; ls ~/Library/LaunchAgents/*goldfish* ~/Library/LaunchAgents/*Goldfish* 2>/dev/null; echo "---"; ls /Library/LaunchAgents/*goldfish* /Library/LaunchAgents/*Goldfish* /Library/LaunchDaemons/*goldfish* /Library/LaunchDaemons/*Goldfish* 2>/dev/null
launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.kaspi.goldfish.autostart 2>/dev/null || launchctl list com.kaspi.goldfish.autostart 2>/dev/null
input.description: Get details on Goldfish launch agent

content.text:
Found it. Goldfish is registered as a **macOS Login Item** via the Service Management framework (`com.apple.xpc.ServiceManagement`), and it has `runatload` enabled. This means macOS will automatically launch it at login, and the `successful exit => 0` semaphore means **macOS will restart it whenever it exits cleanly** (exit code 0).

Here's what's happening:

1. **`com.kaspi.goldfish.autostart`** is a submitted launch agent managed by macOS's Login Items system
2. It has the **`runatload`** property — so it starts on login
3. The semaphore **`successful exit => 0`** tells launchd to relaunch the process whenever it exits with code 0 (i.e., a normal quit)

### How to stop it from restarting

**Option 1 — Disable via System Settings (recommended):**
Go to **System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions** and toggle off **Goldfish**.

**Option 2 — Disable via terminal:**
```bash
launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.kaspi.goldfish.autostart
```

This will stop it for the current session. To prevent it from coming back on next login, use the System Settings method.

All done — the root cause is identified. To summarize:

**Goldfish keeps restarting because it's registered as a macOS Login Item** (`com.kaspi.goldfish.autostart`) with a `successful exit` semaphore, which tells launchd to relaunch it every time it quits cleanly.

The easiest fix is to go to **System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions** and toggle Goldfish off. That will stop macOS from relaunching it.
